 QQQ After A -6.7% October: What History Says About November
 Nov 02, 2026, 4:43 AM ET State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) , DIA , QQQ , IVV , VOO , IWM , SPX , SP500 , NDX , DJI , RTY NVDA , VIX 19 Comments 2 Likes Ang Shen 435 Followers Follow Summary
 QQQ historically delivers its strongest returns in November, with a high probability of rapid recovery after October drawdowns.
 Current S&P 500 fundamentals show no bubble: Q3 earnings up 29.5% YoY, forward P/E at 18.7, below 5- and 10-year averages.
 Buying QQQ after a 10–15% drawdown offers an excellent risk/reward, especially post-midterm elections when uncertainty fades.
 VIX typically drops 12% in November, supporting a positive market outlook and double-digit 12-month gains following midterm elections.
 by-studio/iStock via Getty Images
 Historically speaking, November is the best-performing month for QQQ .
 Usually, the Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ETF ( QQQ ), has, on average, 2.2 drawdowns of 10%+ in a year. This year we may have three 10%+ drawdowns. This is perfectly normal. VIX
